audit.note: REVIEW-21 F2 CORRECTION. The claim above was FALSE AS A COLLECTIVE RATIONALE and is corrected here rather than restated. Audited BY PROPERTY, not by filename: for each entry the vehicle it used was resolved to the case that vehicle points at TODAY. EIGHT of the 23 entries had a SURVIVING vehicle, so "no surviving case carries it" was never true of them. Ruling 65 withdrew per-test paperwork; it did not authorise replacing the packet's no-coverage-loss boundary with a collective rationale that does not hold.
audit.restoration_attempted_and_what_it_showed: Vehicle survival is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT, which the attempt measured rather than assumed. Restoring the five c09_t8 entries against the surviving vehicle produced 16 failures: they also assert the DELETED data's shape (embedded numeric grammar forms, pattern rows, bank structure) and one hardcodes structures/ncaf.edi. Restoring them is a rewrite of the assertions or a re-addition of corpus data, not a repoint. test_c09_t9_machine_error_record_stays_on_stdout uses NO corpus case at all and restores cleanly as source, but then FAILS I20: it deliberately fits an INVALID project to assert the machine error record, and I20 admits only a corpus case. Restoring that property therefore requires an I20 provision for deliberately-invalid projects, or asserting the record without reaching fit — a decision, not an edit, and NOT something to obtain by loosening I20.
